title.narrative: Accelerating the Climate Transition for Green, Inclusive, and Resilient Economic Growth Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative:
The proposed Accelerating the Climate Transition (the Program) supports Uzbekistan to strengthen the enabling environment and institutional arrangements for a climate transition, strengthening the links and interaction of climate change adaptation priorities, and accelerating climate change mitigation actions. The Program aligns with the Asian Development Bank's (ADB) forthcoming Country Partnership Strategy for Uzbekistan, 2024-2028, which prioritizes the facilitation of Uzbekistan's transitioning to a green economy, supports climate change mitigation and adaptation, and climate and disaster resilience. The proposed program complements ADB forthcoming policy-based and sector development programs supporting climate transition in finance and energy.
The Program aligns with ADB Strategy 2030 operational priorities 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 for accelerating progress in gender equality, climate change, resilience, and environment, strengthening governance and institutional capacity, and promoting regional cooperation and integration. The Program is consistent with the ADB Climate Change Action Plan, 2023-2030, which outlines ADB's support for strategic interventions and initiatives to spearhead climate action, in line with the Paris Agreement, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction. Based on the Joint MDB Methodological Approach for Assessment of Paris Agreement Alignment, the Program is aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. To establish clear institutional responsibility and coordination for climate change policy, adaptation and mitigation through a whole of society approach, the government: (i) established the Climate Council under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan; (ii) established the National Government Agency for Green Transformation and Adaptation to Climate Change (Climate Center) under the Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection, and Climate Change; and (iii) adopted a National Climate Policy and Climate Change Gender Action Plan.

1.2. To integrate climate into public financial management, the government: (i) integrated gender and climate into the medium-term fiscal strategy; (ii) mainstreamed climate and gender priorities into medium-term budget framework; (iii) adopted program-based budgeting incorporating climate and gender related outcome indicators; (iv) required climate impacts to be assessed for public investment management encompassing project screening, appraisal, and approval process; and (v) incorporated and disclosed climate fiscal risks in the Fiscal Risk Statement.
19 Nov 2024 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-approves-250-million-loan-support-uzbekistan-green-inclusive-resilient-economic-growth

2.1. In line with the Water Resources Development Concept, 2020-2030 for an integrated approach to climate smart water resource management and conservation, the government: (i) submitted to Parliament the Water Code unifying legal acts and norms in water resource use and protection; and (ii) adopted the Water Resource Management and Irrigation Sector Development Strategy, 2024-2026.

2.2. To address the deficiency in soil management to combat the negative impact of climate change, land degradation, and to increase agricultural productivity, the government (i) enacted the Law About Soil Protection and Increasing Its Productivity (2023) establishing the institutional responsibilities for soil management; the rights and obligations of landowners, land users, and land tenants; and the legal foundation for curbing excessive chemical usage, and promoting regenerative agricultural practices to increase soil fertility for irrigated land; and (ii) adopted a unified methodology for classifying pastures and assessing degradation of pasture lands.

3.1. To unlock green finance for state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and improve the availability of reliable and comparable information on sustainability risks and opportunities, the government required SOEs under the supervision of UzAssets to adopt a National Sustainability Standards Framework comprising (i) the IFRS S1 on sustainability-related financial disclosures, (ii) IFRS S2 on climate-related disclosures; and (iii) Global Reporting Initiative framework for environmental, social, and governance reporting.

3.2. To reduce greenhouse gas emissions through catalyzing a sustainable shift towards e-mobility in public transport, the government approved the Concept of E-Mobility Development of the Republic of Uzbekistan, encompassing the regulatory frameworks, infrastructure development, technology adoption and upskilling, research and development, and a gender action plan.

3.3. To encourage energy conservation and reduce GHG emissions, the Law on Tax and Budget Policy, 2024 was amended to (i) implement advance disposal fees for tires with high environmental disposal costs; (ii) apply a heavy vehicles use tax on freight vehicles and trailers on highways responsible for emitting a rising amount of greenhouse gases; (iii) introduction of “green energy” certificates used to confirm the production of electricity using renewable energy sources; and the 2024 Law on Rationale Use of Energy, Increasing Energy Efficiency, and Energy Conservation was adopted, which sets out a framework for energy conservation and efficiency across economic sectors.
